argument:
The bull correctly quantifies Maybank's starting cushion: CET1 15.657% and total capital 19.413% make the income case materially stronger than an unsupported capital assumption. At 11.51x earnings and 6.2% reported yield, rapid growth is unnecessary for a plausible ownership return. Yet both capital ratios declined and precede the proposed dividend deduction.

Gross impaired loans increased to RM9.362bn from RM8.810bn, while operating income fell to RM14.611bn from RM15.397bn. Cost restraint preserved earnings, but sustained revenue erosion or credit charges could offset income compensation. One-basis-point net-impairment movement is reassuring without cancelling that gross trend. Negative momentum supports measured entry rather than a credit-crisis forecast. The bull answers immediate capital capacity; the remaining reason against aggressive buying is simultaneous income and capital deterioration, not uncertainty alone.
key_points: Measured capital makes the income thesis credible.
Gross impairment and operating-income trends remain adverse.
Yield can compensate risk but is not guaranteed total return.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers capital availability and rejects a growth-dependent thesis persuasively. It has not reversed the observed income and gross-credit deterioration; those trends limit conviction without invalidating every income purchase.
